coaching.title: Easy 4mi Z2 Rolling
coaching.message: Calendar has you down for 4 miles easy on rolling terrain, ~700 ft of gain, HR 138-150. You're 28 days out — taper territory — so this is a volume-light, quality-intact day. Aguas Calientes sits around 2,000m and you came down from Cusco, so your legs will feel better than they did at 3,400m but don't chase pace. Hike the steep pitches deliberately with hands on quads: that's the exact motor you'll need on the Julian Alps climbs. Second 'Run' block at 14:30 and gym at 18:00 — if you do all three, keep the afternoon run to shakeout only and make the gym session light and movement-focused, not heavy. Taper means the work is already in the bank.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Short session, so no in-run fuel needed on the 4 miler — but this is a perfect low-stakes day to sip a 60g/hr carb mix anyway and keep the gut trained for race demands. Peru travel is dehydrating and altitude blunts thirst: front-load 500ml with electrolytes before first light. Post-run, 25-30g protein plus real carbs within the hour. Aim for roughly 220g carbs across the day given the light load, and lean on local staples — potatoes, rice, quinoa — which are everywhere and easy on the stomach.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: You've got a flight, a hotel change, and three activity blocks stacked today — travel load is real training stress even when the mileage is small. Ten minutes of calf and hip flexor work after the descent portion of the run, then legs up the wall for five minutes before dinner. Protect the sleep: you're in taper, and sleep is where the fitness you've already built consolidates. Target 8 hours tonight, no exceptions.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Four weeks out is where fit athletes get restless and start adding work they don't need. Resist it. The taper only fails when you fight it. Use today's rolling terrain as a rehearsal: pick a climb, settle your breathing, and practice the calm you want at kilometer 30 in the Julian Alps. Confidence at this stage comes from executing small sessions cleanly, not from proving anything.
